payload.viable_set: Two viable candidates survive: K2 VENDOR (a proven QR library, source-copied) leads; K1 HAND-ROLL (a minimal zero-dep encoder) is the recorded fallback if the vendored library fails the ship dependency-review. The killer holds - a real alternative survives.
payload.complete_allocation: Both candidates allocate ALL functions - Trigger, Generate, Persist, Encode, Present, Preserve-install/boundary. They differ ONLY in Encode (hand-rolled vs vendored). Interfaces: the connect-flow pipeline (Trigger->Generate->Persist->Encode->Present) + the Encode boundary (input = topic string, output = QR matrix, no external edge). Rationale per candidate in the shortlist.
payload.criteria_traced: Weights derived from requirements + tensions: Scannability (.30) from R3 (a wrong matrix is unusable); Install-simplicity (.25) from R4 + adr-install-over-zerodep; Secrecy-safe (.20) from R2; Least-code (.15) from maintainability; Time-to-build (.10) from affordability.
payload.front_recorded: Front = {K1, K2}. K2 leads (4.50) and wins scannability + time; K1 (3.65) is non-dominated only on install-simplicity, kept as the zero-dep fallback. Eliminated: A3 npm-install (risks one-click install), B2 non-atomic write (violates R5).
payload.feasibility_checked: K2: small proven QR libraries exist that encode byte mode with ECC in a few hundred lines of vendorable source, no runtime deps - feasible, the mainstream path. K1: a correct minimal QR encoder is feasible but demanding (Reed-Solomon ECC + masking + format info) and must be proven scannable by our own tests - feasible, higher risk. Both clear rough feasibility.
